references.text: Moses appoints leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, in accordance with Jethro's advice to organize the people with capable men.
Judges and overseers are to be appointed over the tribes, reflecting the structure Jethro recommended.
Joseph says he fears God, an example of godly fear that Jethro highlights as a necessary quality for leaders.
Nehemiah appointed trustworthy men to have responsibility, which reflects the requirement for truthful men.
He who hates gain shall live – this mirrors the requirement to hate unjust gain.
The apostles choose men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and wisdom, to serve – qualifications similar to those Jethro described.
Paul describes the qualifications for overseers, including that they must not be greedy for money, which corresponds to hating unjust gain.
Elders must be blameless and not greedy for shameful gain, in line with Jethro's requirements for leaders.
Prohibition against taking bribes, because it blinds the eyes – this elaborates on the requirement to hate unjust gain.
The king shall not accumulate silver and gold in large quantities, a principle that supports the requirement for leaders who hate gain.
These are parallel accounts of the same event; Deuteronomy confirms and expands upon the criteria from Exodus.
This text describes the actual implementation of the system proposed in Exodus 18:21.
Proverbs 8:13 defines theologically what 'fearing God' and 'hating evil' (the requirement in Exodus) actually means.
